segments.text: Snow is piling up all over the yard.
Gumgumi catches a single falling snowflake.
This one snowflake is clear as glass.
But the whole snow pile looks pure white.
A single ice crystal lets light pass straight through.
Stack them up, and countless ice-air boundaries appear.
Light bounces off each boundary and scatters everywhere.
Ice doesn't favor any color, so they all scatter evenly.
So all those colors mix back into white light.
That's why snow looks pure white.
